tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk that is not on top, relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs, ensuring they are not placed on the destination peg if they would block the target disk. This clears the path for the larger disk to move legally.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a disk you need to move is buried under smaller disks on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 0 with disks 2 and 1 above, first move disk 1 then disk 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Empty or Larger-Top Pegs for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk may be moved onto any peg that is empty or whose top disk is larger; use such pegs to hold smaller disks temporarily while larger disks are positioned. Choosing an appropriate temporary peg prevents illegal placements.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to free a peg or relocate a disk without violating size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 2 onto an empty peg 2 or onto peg 1 whose top is disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When assembling the final configuration on a goal peg, place disks from largest to smallest, always ensuring the moving disk is smaller than the current top of the goal peg. This guarantees the correct decreasing size order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the final phase of moving all disks onto the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5, place disk 4, then disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1 on the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve sub‑problems by moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the kth (largest) disk to the goal, then moving the k‑1 disks from auxiliary onto the goal, respecting the same rules recursively. This recursive phase planning mirrors the classic Tower of Hanoi algorithm.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of several disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg A to C using B: move 1‑2 to B, move 3 to C, then move 1‑2 from B to C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Avoid moving a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must be below it have been placed; otherwise the larger disk cannot be moved later. Delaying small disks prevents blocking the construction of the final stack.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already contains some larger disks but not the full stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not move disk 1 onto peg 2 before disk 4 has been placed there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Each move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost on its peg, and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. Checking these conditions before each move ensures legality.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg 1’s top is disk 2, you cannot move disk 3 onto peg 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already holds correctly ordered larger disks, keep them untouched and only add smaller disks on top, never moving the existing base disks. Treating them as a fixed base simplifies planning.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal configuration is partially satisfied at the start.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Disk 5 is already on peg 2; never move it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be moved to any peg without breaking size rules; use it to unblock other disks or to swap positions. Its flexibility makes it a useful temporary placeholder.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary move to free a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg 2 to free disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid Temporary Blocking Stacks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not create temporary stacks where a larger disk sits on a smaller one unless you plan to dismantle that stack before the larger disk needs to move again. Such blocking stacks can make later moves impossible.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When choosing where to place a disk temporarily.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Avoid moving disk 3 onto peg 2 if disk 4 still needs to be placed there later.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to confirm that every move is legal and the final state matches the goal; correct any discrepancy before output. This post‑construction verification catches errors early.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have written the complete sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Replay the moves to ensure peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1].
